title: Choose the AidOS visual world (re-roll 1)
question: The re-roll assigned Emergency Wayfinding: public safety signage, where every panel says exactly one thing and its colour carries the meaning. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Emergency Wayfinding
options.lineage: ISO 7010 / ISO 3864 safety signs and evacuation wayfinding
options.thesis: AidOS reads like a public emergency sign system: each panel states one fact, safety colours carry meaning, and the product is a route you follow.
options.viewport: An overhead navy directory sign carries the headline and lists the demo scenario's zones and requests like a station board; the primary action is a green directional panel with an arrow.
options.risk: Can tip into building-safety poster if signal colours decorate instead of meaning something.

raised.raise: One decisive control (the scenario selector) re-sets every sign on the dashboard at once.
Colour is reserved for the item whose state matters now; resting panels stay navy and sign-blank.
One strict grid governs both pages: every plate snaps to the same column and baseline system.
Signal intensity scales with urgency: more saturated ink only where shortfall or criticality rises.
Empty and planned states read as visible blank plates with a label, never as missing space.

options.label: Waybill in Triplicate
options.lineage: relief-cargo waybills and carbon-copy dispatch forms
options.thesis: Every plan is a form in triplicate: the candidate copy, the committed copy, and the archive copy are the state machine.
options.viewport: A dispatch waybill with form boxes for depot and zones; COMMITTED and CANDIDATE stamps mark plan state.
options.risk: Familiar paperwork pastiche; stamps and pastel copies can feel bureaucratic rather than calm.

options.label: Darkroom Safelight
options.thesis: Allocation as a print: fixed stations, a test strip previews the plan, and commit is irreversible past a marked point.
options.viewport: A station strip (load, score, allocate, compare, commit) under amber light, the plan emerging like a print.
options.case: Maps the FSM perfectly (test strip = candidate, fix = commit), but markers do not see emergency logistics in a darkroom.
options.risk: An amber ground fights amber as the warning colour, and the mood reads moody rather than calm.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One cord pulls a flat plane into protective volume.
options.viewport: A black semicircle that gathers when the cord is pulled.
options.risk: Luxury fashion register; nothing a coordinator recognises.
options.kept: One decisive control transforms the whole state.

options.label: Paper Automata
options.thesis: A crank turns a procession of paper figures.
options.viewport: A procession of folded figures along a crank line.
options.kept: One colour reserved for the item currently changing.

options.label: ASCII Live Render
options.thesis: A scene drawn in glyph density.
options.viewport: A rotating glyph scene on black.
options.kept: One strict grid as the whole composition.

options.label: Solidarity Silkscreen
options.thesis: Flat colour fields around one emblem, slogan repeated in four languages.
options.viewport: A centred emblem framed by a running multilingual slogan.
options.risk: Political poster register and a cream ground; poor for data.
options.case: Holds some humanitarian resonance but loses product clarity.
options.kept: Ink intensity rises with urgency and calms back to two inks.

options.label: Console Void
options.thesis: Floating memory towers in a dark void.
options.kept: Empty slots stay visible as hollows.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A navy SaaS landing page: headline left, dashboard screenshot right, feature cards below.
canonCard.viewport: Split hero with copy beside a dashboard mock, then a row of feature cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any other analytics product by design.
